title: Does a longer boundary mean more space inside?
description: A thin ten centimetre by one centimetre strip is set beside a five centimetre by four centimetre rectangle, and the perimeter and the area of each are worked out. The strip has the longer boundary but covers less. Keeko doubts this and says the longer boundary must cover more.
teaching_notes: One idea: perimeter measures the boundary and area counts the unit squares inside, so one can grow while the other shrinks. Watch for children who think a longer perimeter means a larger area.

source: Compare a 10 cm by 1 cm strip with a 5 cm by 4 cm rectangle:
video_script.why: The child sees that perimeter cannot stand in for area, because two rectangles can have the longer boundary and the smaller area.
video_script.substitution: Work out the perimeter and the area of each rectangle separately, then compare the two perimeters and the two areas.
video_script.anchor: the strip and the rectangle that show perimeter and area disagreeing
video_script.wrong_answer: the strip covers more because its border is longer
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads a longer boundary as more space inside. Counting unit squares gives the strip 10 and the rectangle 20.
video_script.payoff_line: the strip has the larger perimeter but the smaller area

final_answer.value: The strip has the larger perimeter (22 cm) but the smaller area (10 cm²)
final_answer.spoken: twenty two centimetres against eighteen, and ten square centimetres against twenty

hold_back: the strip has the larger perimeter but the smaller area
never_show: which shape has the larger perimeter or area, before the compare step
maths_rules: strip 10 cm by 1 cm: perimeter 2 × (10 + 1) = 2 × 11 = 22 cm; area 10 × 1 = 10 cm²
rectangle 5 cm by 4 cm: perimeter 2 × (5 + 4) = 2 × 9 = 18 cm; area 5 × 4 = 20 cm²
video_script.design: One idea: perimeter counts the boundary, area counts the squares inside. Wrong idea: a longer boundary means more space. The strip and the rectangle stay on stage from the hook to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The strip has the larger perimeter but the smaller area.
Its perimeter is twenty two centimetres against eighteen, and its area is ten square centimetres against twenty.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the strip covers more because its border is longer.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Count the squares inside. The strip holds ten and the rectangle holds twenty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A longer boundary does not promise a bigger inside, so perimeter cannot measure area.
